control: BLIND CONTROL — do not tune against this file. Do not read a number out of it while a SKILL.md is open, and do not quote a per-skill delta from it in any brief that also proposes an edit. These eleven cases were authored from each skill's SKILL.md, its coverage-matrix.md and scenarios/registry.yaml, never from a measured result, and they are the only thing in this repository that can tell an improvement from an overfit. Reading these results to guide an edit SPENDS this control, exactly as iteration 3 spent the last one, and the iteration that spends it owes the next one a replacement set authored the same way. Say what that costs, because the cost is now the point: this is the THIRD corpus (evals.json tuned, regression.json spent, this one blind), and an eval programme that burns a control per iteration is not sustainable — every replacement is authored by someone who has already read the failure it is supposed to be blind to, the authoring cost recurs every iteration, and the supply of untouched scenarios and fixtures is finite. A future iteration should rotate a portion instead of replacing wholesale: retire and re-author only the two or three skills whose results actually steered an edit, and leave the rest sealed.

evals.prompt: Triage for the tracker, please. Finding as our incident lead wrote it: 'Upstream's publisher account was taken over on the 14th. They published 2.4.1 under the legitimate signing key, and our agent host applied that update automatically within the hour with no human review.' I need one origin AST id, any contributing entries with an owner and an action against each, the queue to send it to, and a date by which the scan will confirm it — our tracker only closes a ticket as 'confirmed' or 'false positive', so I need to know which one this is heading for.
evals.expected_output: AST02 is the single origin: a distribution path admitted the artifact, and the takeover is the fix that would have prevented the finding. AST07 is recorded as a contributing control failure, with an owner — the installing organisation's update policy — and an action, a verification gate on the update path that routes substantive changes to a human rather than auto-applying whatever upstream published. Two owners, two actions, one origin. What the request cannot have is a confirmation date. Nothing in triage opens the package under discussion, so 'routed to' is the strongest verb available here and 'confirmed as' belongs to the target once it has run something. In this particular routing neither category has anything to run: Maintainer Account Takeover is one of the three AST02 scenarios no package decides — AST02's only in-package verdict is config-file hijacking — and AST07 ships no detector, no fixture case and no F1 at all. So both the hand-off and the contributing entry go to a named person and a named process rather than to a scan queue, and that has to be said before anyone runs anything, so a silence from an empty tier is never read back as a clean result. The two closure options on offer do not include the correct outcome; say so rather than picking the nearer one, because a ticket closed pending a scan that will never run is worse than an open ticket.
assertions: The response gives AST02 as the single origin and records AST07 as a contributing control failure carrying its own owner and action, rather than as a second primary.
The response refuses to supply a date by which a scan will confirm the finding, and gives the reason that nothing in triage opens the package, so 'routed to' is the strongest claim available.

The response states that neither the origin nor the contributing category has a check that could confirm this finding — maintainer account takeover is not decidable from a package, and AST07 ships no detector and no F1 — so the hand-off is to a named person and process rather than to a scan queue.
The response declines the tracker's two closure options instead of choosing the nearer one, and says a ticket closed pending a scan that will never run is worse than an open ticket.
